BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary points

- **I have reviewed every clause, including those the Seller marks [STANDARD].** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" says [STANDARD] items have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides." Nothing in our file shows that. Under our playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3), labels such as "standard," "market," "FINAL," "settled," "agreed," or "not intended to be re-opened" do not bind us. They have to be confirmed through our own authority process.
- **Matching a fallback number does not clear a clause.** The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period both match our conditional fallbacks. Neither fallback has been authorised, and the package is worse than our position in many other respects, so neither number can be accepted on its own.
- **Some facts are dated.** The disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Before we respond, the deal team should refresh the status of Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006 and the Sandbar renewals.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Departure |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft (none given) | Below our opening position and unauthorised |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our threshold |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, then excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | Converts a tipping basket into a deductible, roughly 5x higher |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval (none given) | Unauthorised reduction |
| Limitation cross-application (cl 12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Hidden override that would reach title, tax, IP and fraud claims |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Core departure |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent; no waiver | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), public registers, Accounts, statutory registers | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Deemed disclosure of everything in the data room |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excludes title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion, including constructive knowledge |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Consent-on-delivery. DL 2 confirms no final consent or condition evidence exists |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3) | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Post-Completion release of security. DL 3 confirms about AUD 3.2m is unpaid |
| Bonuses (funds flow; DL 5) | AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; no silent exclusion | Silent exclusion. On-costs unquantified |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) | Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified | Narrow indemnity |
| DD-006 export/privacy (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Characterisation not supported by DL 6, which says scope and notification are unknown |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Asserted classification. DL 8 says it cannot confirm the position |
| Tax/IP (Seller note) | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Treats open categories as closed and subject to the general regime |
| Title (Seller note; DL 10) | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Relies on an internal source |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a) Structural package (caps, baskets, time limits).** Taken together, the Seller's general regime cuts the economic value of general warranty claims substantially. A AUD 250,000 deductible basket and a AUD 25,000 de minimis mean small and medium claims may be irrecoverable. Combined with the 18-month period, the Seller is seeking to reduce recovery across all dimensions. Our position is 25% / AUD 6m, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, and 24 months.

**b) Fundamental and title claims folded into the general regime.** This is the most serious structural issue. Title and capacity are fundamental to what we are buying. Subjecting them to a 20% cap, a basket and an 18-month window would leave us exposed to title defects discovered later. This conflicts with our separate regime (100% cap, six years, outside the basket and knowledge bar). Combined with the "any limitation applies to all Claims" language, the Seller could argue that the general limits extend to title, tax and IP claims. We should reject the cross-application expressly.

**c) Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's blanket application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" is not acceptable. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this. This should be presented as a non-negotiable drafting point.

**d) Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** The Seller combines whole-data-room deemed disclosure (DL 1.1) with a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) that covers anything "discoverable" from the data room. Together, these would convert the entire data room into disclosure against the warranties. Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure only, and the knowledge exclusion should be deleted or limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity claims. The DL 1.4 non-admission is acceptable as drafted, but it does not change our conditions.

**e) Completion-critical consents and debt.**
- **Bluefen:** About AUD 3.6m (roughly 30%) of FY26 revenue depends on the change-control consent (DL 2). The Seller's proposal to treat consent as satisfied on delivery, under reasonable endeavours, is inconsistent with our requirement that effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions be in hand before Completion. Our position is that a material customer consent cannot rest on reasonable endeavours alone.
- **Riverlark:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unpaid (DL 3). Post-Completion release of security is not acceptable without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Our requirement is repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.

**f) Funds flow and bonuses.** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs) are excluded from the draft funds flow and described as "a matter for the Seller." That is not enough. Either the amount must be a specific line item or the Seller must fund it. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not quantified in DL 5 and need to be included in the mechanism. We should confirm with counsel whether the employment conditions and any Completion-triggered payments create any further liability.

**g) Ironquay IP.** The indemnity covers only the AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment. The DL 4 position is that no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified, so we should not treat it as either confirmed or resolved. The indemnity should be broadened to cover the IP transfer and ownership risk, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.

**h) DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller's description ("not expected to be material") is more confident than DL 6 allows. DL 6 says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown, and it is unclear whether an unauthorised person accessed the file or whether notification is required. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) are involved. Our playbook says to assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. The practical steps are:
- require preservation of logs and an investigation timetable;
- require regular updates until the investigation closes;
- obtain privacy counsel's view on notification obligations under the Privacy Act, without assuming a conclusion either way.

Whether a specific indemnity is needed for this matter is a principal-level decision. It is not a playbook position, so it should be referred to Amelia Frost rather than proposed as settled.

**i) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says the disclosure does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together because the three renewals may overlap in timing or scope. Our playbook requires assessment only, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.

**j) Office lease and Mossvale (DL 7, DL 9).** The playbook does not address these directly. DL 7 and DL 9 both say the materials do not establish that landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. We should not accept that as a conclusion. The deal team should confirm whether either counterparty must consent or be notified before Completion and, if so, bring them into the consent conditions.

**k) Title.** The DD-012 register is an internal source supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof of title, encumbrances or authority. Our requirement is independent evidence: ASIC company extracts, PPSR and other security searches, and evidence of corporate authority for the Seller. DL 10 itself acknowledges that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**l) Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our playbook keeps them open, and we should not assume unlimited liability or resolution. They should be dealt with in their own categories.

## 3. Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. The Seller's "FINAL / not re-opened / cleared" framing. Our position is that nothing is cleared until our authority process confirms it.
2. Folding title, capacity, tax and IP into the general regime, and the blanket cross-application of limitations.
3. The absence of a fraud carve-out.
4. Whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts-based deemed disclosure.
5. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in cl 8.3.
6. Consent-on-delivery for Bluefen.
7. Post-Completion Riverlark release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. The silent exclusion of the AUD 420,000 bonuses from the funds flow.
9. The narrow Ironquay indemnity.
10. Treating the Sandbar renewals as ordinary course or Debt by default.

**Counter-propose (in line with the playbook):**
- General cap: 25% / AUD 6m.
- De minimis: AUD 5,000. Basket: AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months.
- Fundamental/title: separate regime with 100% cap and at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Specific fair disclosure only.
- Knowledge qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry.
- Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.
- Riverlark: repayment and security releases from Completion funds.
- Bonuses: specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs.
- Ironquay: broadened indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure.
- DD-006: preservation, investigation and updates. No numeric demand and no confirmed-breach characterisation.
- Sandbar: assess only.
- Title: independent searches and authority evidence.

**Escalate to Amelia Frost (principal decisions):**
- Whether to offer the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap or the 18-month period as conditional fallbacks. Neither may be offered without her written authority identifying the draft.
- Whether to request a specific indemnity for DD-006.
- Any tax or IP positions, which remain open.

**Information requests to the Seller:**
- Current status of the Bluefen consent and its conditions.
- Current Riverlark payout figure and draft release documents.
- The DD-005 bonus calculation, including on-costs, and the employment conditions.
- Ironquay SOW3 payment status, receipt evidence or confirmatory assignment.
- DD-006 investigation scope, log preservation confirmation and timetable.
- The three Sandbar renewal contracts, with terms, termination rights and timing.
- Whether the office lease and Mossvale arrangements require consent or notice.
- Independent title and encumbrance evidence, including corporate authority for the Seller.

**Before we respond:** Refresh the facts as at today's date, since the disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Confirm statutory points (Privacy Act notification, payroll tax and superannuation on-costs, lease and Mossvale consent requirements) with NSW counsel before we rely on any of them in the mark-up.

Either the amount must be a specific line item or the Seller must fund it. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not quantified in DL 5 and need to be included in the mechanism. We should confirm with counsel whether the employment conditions and any Completion-triggered payments create any further liability.

**g) Ironquay IP.** The indemnity covers only the AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment. The DL 4 position is that no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified, so we should not treat it as either confirmed or resolved. The indemnity should be broadened to cover the IP transfer and ownership risk, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.

**h) DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller's description ("not expected to be material") is more confident than DL 6 allows. DL 6 says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown, and it is unclear whether an unauthorised person accessed the file or whether notification is required. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) are involved. Our playbook says to assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. The practical steps are:
- require preservation of logs and an investigation timetable;
- require regular updates until the investigation closes;
- obtain privacy counsel's view on notification obligations under the Privacy Act, without assuming a conclusion either way.

Whether a specific indemnity is needed for this matter is a principal-level decision. It is not a playbook position, so it should be referred to Amelia Frost rather than proposed as settled.

**i) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says the disclosure does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together because the three renewals may overlap in timing or scope. Our playbook requires assessment only, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.

**j) Office lease and Mossvale (DL 7, DL 9).** The playbook does not address these directly. DL 7 and DL 9 both say the materials do not establish that landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. We should not accept that as a conclusion. The deal team should confirm whether either counterparty must consent or be notified before Completion and, if so, bring them into the consent conditions.

**k) Title.** The DD-012 register is an internal source supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof of title, encumbrances or authority. Our requirement is independent evidence: ASIC company extracts, PPSR and other security searches, and evidence of corporate authority for the Seller. DL 10 itself acknowledges that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**l) Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our playbook keeps them open, and we should not assume unlimited liability or resolution. They should be dealt with in their own categories.

## 3. Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. The Seller's "FINAL / not re-opened / cleared" framing. Our position is that nothing is cleared until our authority process confirms it.
2. Folding title, capacity, tax and IP into the general regime, and the blanket cross-application of limitations.
3. The absence of a fraud carve-out.
4. Whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts-based deemed disclosure.
5. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in cl 8.3.
6. Consent-on-delivery for Bluefen.
7. Post-Completion Riverlark release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. The silent exclusion of the AUD 420,000 bonuses from the funds flow.
9. The narrow Ironquay indemnity.
10. Treating the Sandbar renewals as ordinary course or Debt by default.

**Counter-propose (in line with the playbook):**
- General cap: 25% / AUD 6m.
- De minimis: AUD 5,000. Basket: AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months.
- Fundamental/title: separate regime with 100% cap and at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Specific fair disclosure only.
- Knowledge qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry.
- Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.
- Riverlark: repayment and security releases from Completion funds.
- Bonuses: specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs.
- Ironquay: broadened indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure.
- DD-006: preservation, investigation and updates. No numeric demand and no confirmed-breach characterisation.
- Sandbar: assess only.
- Title: independent searches and authority evidence.

**Escalate to Amelia Frost (principal decisions):**
- Whether to offer the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap or the 18-month period as conditional fallbacks. Neither may be offered without her written authority identifying the draft.
- Whether to request a specific indemnity for DD-006.
- Any tax or IP positions, which remain open.

**Information requests to the Seller:**
- Current status of the Bluefen consent and its conditions.
- Current Riverlark payout figure and draft release documents.
- The DD-005 bonus calculation, including on-costs, and the employment conditions.
- Ironquay SOW3 payment status, receipt evidence or confirmatory assignment.
- DD-006 investigation scope, log preservation confirmation and timetable.
- The three Sandbar renewal contracts, with terms, termination rights and timing.
- Whether the office lease and Mossvale arrangements require consent or notice.
- Independent title and encumbrance evidence, including corporate authority for the Seller.

**Before we respond:** Refresh the facts as at today's date, since the disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Confirm statutory points (Privacy Act notification, payroll tax and superannuation on-costs, lease and Mossvale consent requirements) with NSW counsel before we rely on any of them in the mark-up.
